To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
N-lauroyl sarcosine (NLA) and linseed oil, when used together in a nanocomposite microcontainer, can be used for improving the corrosion resistance of waterborne acrylic coatings.
the ASC coatings with NLS microcontainers have improved adhesion properties to the substrate, and the protective properties of the coatings were improved in case of damage.
NLS microcontainers filled with LO can be used for increasing the protective properties of ASC coatings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the development of self-healing coatings with the inhibition properties.
the development of a new approach of the corrosion protection of metals by the use of nanocomposite coatings and the use of nanotechnology for the improvement of their performance.
the development of biofriendly nanocomposite coatings with self-healing properties and with the inhibition of corrosion processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of microcontainers filled with LO and containing NLS as a corrosion inhibitor can be considered as a promising approach to the improvement of protective performance of ASC coatings, but only when their integrity is damaged.

ASC coatings containing LO and NLS in a form of micro-containers can be used for protection of low-carbon steel surfaces from corrosion in neutral salt spray conditions, but the protective properties are not as effective as for the coatings containing free NLS powder.

the application of the microcontainers filled with linseed oil and N-lauroyl sarcosine as a corrosion inhibitor in the coatings based on acryl-stayrene copolymer is a promising way for the improvement of protective properties of coatings.

the use of microcontainers filled with NLS in ASC coatings can be considered as a promising approach for improving corrosion resistance of ASC coatings.
ASC-based coatings with incorporated LO and NLS in the form of microcontainers can be considered as promising materials for corrosion protection of steel structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of LO-filled containers in ASC-based coatings is not a good idea.
the combination of two environmentally friendly components, NLS and LO, into a nanocomposite microcontainer can provide a promising solution for the improvement of protective performance of coatings.
the combination of LO and ASC is a promising approach for the development of self-healing protective coatings.
